extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in international affairs (Anglo‑American policy on Palestine)
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing the Anglo‑American committee's findings and recommendations on Jewish immigration to Palestine, the future governance of Palestine, and related political and humanitarian measures, plus domestic and international reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: No domination by one group
rubrics_metrics.description: “That Jew shall not dominate [and] Arab not dominate in Palestine.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the committee's three paramount principles: neither Jews nor Arabs should dominate Palestine politically or institutionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palestine shall be neither a Jewish state nor an Arab state
rubrics_metrics.description: “That Palestine shall be neither a Jewish state nor an Arab state.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee recommended against establishing Palestine exclusively as a Jewish or Arab state; the future status should avoid sole national/religious ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of government with international guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: “That the form of government [shall have] international guarantees, fully protect and preserve the interest in the Holy Land of Christendom and of the Moslem and Jewish faiths.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a governmental structure backed by international guarantees to protect the religious interests and holy places of Christians, Muslims, and Jews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate objective: state protecting rights of all faiths with self-government
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee contended that Palestine should ultimately become a state which guards the rights and interests of Moslems, Jews and Christians alike and, according to the inhabitants as a whole, enjoy the fullest measure of self government consistent with the three paramount principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long‑term aim is a pluralist polity granting broad self‑government while respecting the three core principles (no domination, neither exclusively Jewish nor Arab, international guarantees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical majority not basis for government type
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee argued that numerical majority cannot become the basis for determining the type of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: majority rule is seen as a source of present Arab‑Jewish conflict; government form should avoid being decided solely by population counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate admission of 100,000 displaced European Jews
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that 100,000 homeless European Jews be admitted to Palestine 'as far as possible in 1946.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee endorsed urgent admission of 100,000 refugees to alleviate immediate postwar needs; this was repeatedly highlighted and welcomed by some political leaders, though politically contentious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for admission: displaced persons and liberated populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority should be given to those living in displaced persons centers and those liberated and still living in Germany and Austria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions/Certificates of admission to Palestine were to be prioritized for displaced persons and those liberated from Nazi custody in Central Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award certificates of admission as mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation for the award of 100,000 certificates of admission to Palestine 'as far as possible in 1946.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational mechanism suggested by the committee to effect immediate immigration—issuing formal certificates to refugees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind the 1940 land law
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee recommended rescinding the land law of 1940.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of broader measures to facilitate development and Jewish settlement as well as to address land‑ownership legal barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Palestine and protect holy places
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for developing Palestine and protecting all holy places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee recommended development projects for Palestine alongside guarantees and protections for religious sites of Christianity, Judaism and Islam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee equal civil and religious rights to all inhabitants
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to guarantee equal rights to all inhabitants of Palestine and to ensure complete protection to the Arab population by guaranteeing their civil and religious rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommending measures for constant improvement in the cultural, educational and economic position of the Arab population as part of rights protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to original mandate principle on immigration
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee stood pat on the principle laid down in the original mandate that administration of Palestine should facilitate Jewish immigration under suitable conditions while ensuring the rights and position of other sections are not prejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms continuing the mandate's balancing instruction—encourage Jewish immigration subject to protections for existing non‑Jewish populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed annual immigration maximum or minimum recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee said it would recommend neither a maximum nor minimum for annual immigration in the future, because 'there are too many uncertain factors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaves future annual immigration levels open and contingent on changing circumstances; committee declined to set a numeric annual cap or floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report is advisory / non‑binding
rubrics_metrics.description: The report 'will be binding on no one' and 'the report is not binding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: committee recommendations are advisory and governments remain free to accept, modify or reject them; political implementation is uncertain.
